overview: Manuka Resources is an Australian precious-metals junior developing two 100%-owned, fully permitted mine assets in the Cobar Basin, NSW - the Mt Boppy gold mine and the Wonawinta silver project - which it is restarting in 2026 after a period on care and maintenance. It also owns Trans-Tasman Resources (TTR), whose Taranaki VTM project is a large-scale offshore vanadium-titanium-magnetite iron sands resource in New Zealand's South Taranaki Bight that requires marine consents it does not currently have. Manuka is dual-listed - primary on the ASX (MKR) and a foreign-exempt secondary listing on the NZX (MKR.NZ, quoted in NZD) since 29 September 2025 - and reports in AUD with a 30 June fiscal year end.

business_model.summary: Pre-revenue restart-stage miner: FY2025 and H1FY2026 both recorded zero sales revenue as Mt Boppy and Wonawinta were on care and maintenance. The company is recommissioning the Wonawinta CIL processing plant to generate cash flow from gold ore (from mid-2026) and then silver ore (targeted September 2026 quarter) sold to a single off-taker. The Taranaki VTM project is a separate, much larger, longer-dated optionality asset with no revenue until final consents, financing and construction are achieved - a multi-year process even in the best case.

revenue_streams.name: Taranaki VTM iron/vanadium concentrate (pre-development, no consent)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - single off-taker for gold/silver concentrate/doré; no customers yet for Taranaki VTM
business_model.geographic_mix: Operations 100% in NSW, Australia (Mt Boppy, Wonawinta); Taranaki VTM project 100% in New Zealand's Exclusive Economic Zone; dual ASX/NZX listing

main_competitors: Cobar Basin peers (Peel Mining, Aurelia Metals, Metals Acquisition/CSA)
Silver restart/junior producers (Investigator Resources, Adriatic Metals)
Global VTM/iron-sands and vanadium developers (Trimetals/QMines analogues, South African/Chinese vanadium producers)
Junior gold restart operators in NSW (Alkane Resources, Aurelia Metals)
competitive_position.market_position: Micro-cap (~A$120m market cap) restart-stage precious metals producer with no current market share; Taranaki VTM would be a globally significant vanadium/iron-sands resource (one of the largest drilled vanadium deposits worldwide) if ever permitted and built, but has zero regulatory approval to operate

moat_factors.description: Wonawinta already has a granted mining lease, an existing ~1Mtpa CIL plant, approved tailings dams and accommodation - materially lower capex/time to restart (~A$26.6m) than a greenfield project
No JV partners or royalty overhangs diluting economics, full optionality retained

3.2Bt VTM resource containing 1.6Mt V2O5, ranked among the largest drilled vanadium projects globally, with a granted mining permit - but this scale advantage is neutralized by lack of environmental consent
Vanadium/titanium are on NZ's Critical Minerals List and Fast-track Approvals Act Schedule 2, giving government-level support, though this has not translated into consent approval

weaknesses: No revenue for over two years (FY2025 was the first year in 5 with zero gold or silver output)
Single off-taker concentration for concentrate/doré sales

Taranaki VTM consent was DECLINED in draft form by the Fast-track expert panel (4 Feb 2026) and the application was withdrawn (19 Feb 2026) rather than face a final refusal - the seabed mining path is now materially uncertain with no clear alternative approval route
History of heavy shareholder dilution and debt-for-equity/warrant issuance to fund operations
Small, thinly analyst-covered micro-cap with limited institutional following

growth_drivers: Restart of Wonawinta silver and Mt Boppy gold production in 2026, monetizing existing infrastructure at near-record precious metals prices (silver up ~160% and gold up ~65% in CY2025, with further gains into 2026)
10-year Cobar Basin mine plan (Jan 2026 update) targeting average EBITDA of ~A$127m p.a. at C1 cost of ~A$34.4/oz silver, NPV8 of ~A$805m and IRR of ~1,092% at then-prevailing metal price assumptions
Mt Boppy Open Pit gold cutback and Pipeline Ridge exploration target providing high-grade incremental ounces and multi-year mine life extension
Full drawdown of the US$30m Nebari Natural Resources Credit Fund facility plus recent equity raises intended to fully fund the restart through to first silver production
Unhedged exposure to spot gold and silver prices, both near multi-decade highs, providing operating leverage if the restart executes on time and on budget

Long-dated optionality in the Taranaki VTM project (post-tax NPV10 of US$1.26bn, IRR 39%, average annual EBITDA of US$312m per the PFS) if a viable consenting pathway is eventually found, though this is not embedded in near-term value

business.description: Nearly all near-term value depends on successfully recommissioning one processing plant (Wonawinta) and restarting two mines that have been on care and maintenance for 2+ years; plant modifications (desliming circuit) are unproven at full scale
Company currently delivers all product to a single off-taker

business.risk: Small, unproven reserve base with high Inferred content
business.description: The 10.9Mt Cobar mine plan is underpinned by only 6.9Mt of Reserves and comprises 39% Inferred Resources, with no certainty conversion will occur at forecast grade/tonnage

financial.description: H1FY2026 interim financial statements (31 Dec 2025) explicitly disclose a loss of A$12.9m, operating cash outflow of A$7.7m and net current liabilities of A$21.7m, and state these factors 'indicate a material uncertainty which may cast significant doubt as to whether the Group will continue as a going concern'

New US$30m senior secured Nebari facility (drawn in tranches through June 2026) replaced prior TransAsia debt; substantial finance costs (A$5.5m in H1FY2026 alone, including share-based payments to lenders) and warrants issued to the lender (36.4m warrants at A$0.2004, expiring 2030) add dilution and cash cost

Share capital roughly tripled from A$72.9m to A$105.4m between June and December 2025 via equity raises; ~1.6bn shares now on issue; options/warrants exercises (e.g., 73.4m shares from option exercise post period-end) add further dilution
AUD reporting entity with USD-denominated Nebari facility and NZD-denominated NZX listing/TTR project exposes the company to AUD/USD and AUD/NZD movements

regulatory.description: The Fast-track expert panel's draft decision (4 Feb 2026) proposed declining the marine and discharge consents on environmental/cultural grounds (risk to Māui dolphin, kororā/little penguin, fairy prion, and unproven economic benefit case), and TTR withdrew its application (19 Feb 2026) rather than pursue a likely final refusal. This is the second failed attempt at NZ marine consent for this project (following a 2021 Supreme Court-driven refusal under the EEZ Act), and no clear alternative approval pathway currently exists
Ongoing rehabilitation, tailings and environmental bond obligations at Mt Boppy/Wonawinta

macro.description: Restart economics are highly sensitive to gold/silver prices, which are near record/multi-decade highs; a material pullback would compress the projected EBITDA/IRR materially given the newly built cost base
Reliance on a specialist resource-credit lender (Nebari) at a relatively high effective cost reflects the company's risk profile and limits refinancing optionality

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold and silver prices have both risen sharply through CY2025-26 (silver +~160% in CY2025, gold +~65%, with further gains into 2026) on safe-haven demand, central bank buying and industrial/AI-related silver demand, providing a strong tailwind for restart economics of small-cap precious metals producers. Vanadium/titanium demand is supported by steel alloy and grid-scale battery storage growth, and NZ policy (Critical Minerals List, Fast-track Act, Minerals Strategy 2040) explicitly targets doubling mineral export earnings by 2035 - but seabed/offshore mining faces acute environmental and Māori/iwi cultural opposition in New Zealand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - a junior mining restart story fully exposed to commodity price cycles, with fixed near-term production costs against a variable revenue base once operating
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-high indirectly via the cost and availability of specialist project debt (Nebari facility) and via gold/silver's inverse relationship to real interest rates
key_input_costs: Reagents (cyanide, flotation chemicals) for CIL/flotation processing
Debt servicing costs on the Nebari facility

recent_developments.event: Completed refinance of prior senior secured debt facility (TransAsia); two-tranche capital raising completed with second tranche subject to AGM shareholder approval (granted late Nov 2025)
Commenced trading on the NZX (foreign-exempt secondary listing, code MKR.NZ, quoted in NZD) and released the 10-year Cobar Basin production plan for Wonawinta silver and Mt Boppy gold

Executed and then finalized definitive documentation for a US$30 million senior secured term facility with Nebari Natural Resources Credit Fund II; Tranche 1 (US$26m) drawn 27 Feb 2026, Tranche 2 completed 26 June 2026, fully funding the restart

Released updated 10-year Mine Plan for Wonawinta/Mt Boppy: 10.9Mt production target, average EBITDA ~A$127m p.a. at C1 cost A$34.4/oz silver, NPV8 A$805m, IRR ~1,092%; capex to restart plant raised to A$26.6m (including A$11.4m desliming circuit)

Fast-track expert panel issued a draft decision proposing to DECLINE marine and discharge consents for the Taranaki VTM Project, citing unproven environmental mitigation (risk to Māui dolphin, kororā, fairy prion) and an unconvincing economic benefits case
TTR withdrew its Fast-track application for Taranaki VTM rather than face a near-certain final refusal; company now reviewing options to progress environmental approvals via an alternative pathway
Announced the end of the Care and Maintenance program - officially transitioning to operational mode ahead of restart
H1FY2026 interim results released: A$12.9m half-year loss, A$21.7m net current liabilities, and explicit going-concern material uncertainty disclosure by directors and auditor
First gold processing revenue targeted mid-July 2026 from Wonawinta/Mt Boppy stockpiles; silver production targeted for the September 2026 quarter

guidance.as_of: H1FY2026 interim report (16 March 2026) and 30 January 2026 Mine Plan release

items.notes: From Wonawinta and Mt Boppy stockpile processing
Wonawinta open pit mining scheduled to commence Q3 CY2026 per the 30 Jan 2026 mine plan
Up from the earlier A$18.9m estimate cited in the FY2025 annual report; includes A$11.4m for a new desliming circuit

Up materially from the FY2025 estimate of ~A$22m p.a. at A$50/oz silver, reflecting both an expanded mine plan and higher assumed silver price; C1 cost guided at A$34.4/oz silver including gold credits

items.target: Fully funded through to silver production
items.notes: Combination of A$15m equity raise and fully-drawn US$30m Nebari facility; management states this covers restart through to Wonawinta silver production

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chairman Dennis Karp has repeatedly emphasized that elevated gold and silver prices provide 'fantastic momentum' to the restart plans and that the directors are confident in continuing as a going concern based on the company's history of successfully raising capital since its 2020 IPO, creditor support, and high metal prices. On Taranaki VTM, management states it is 'working through a number of options to progress the final environmental approvals' following the Fast-track withdrawal, but has not disclosed a specific alternative pathway or timeline.

bull_case: Precious metals prices (gold and silver) are near record/multi-decade highs, and Manuka is restarting two previously producing, fully permitted assets with existing infrastructure at a fraction of greenfield capex and lead time

Fully funded restart (equity raise + drawn US$30m Nebari facility) removes near-term financing risk specifically for the Cobar Basin gold/silver restart, with first gold revenue targeted mid-2026 and silver following in Q3 CY2026

10-year mine plan economics are compelling on paper (average EBITDA ~A$127m p.a., NPV8 ~A$805m) if executed at guided costs and current metal prices, which would be transformative relative to the current ~A$120m market cap
100% ownership across all three projects retains full upside optionality without JV dilution, and unhedged production offers maximum leverage to further silver/gold price appreciation

Taranaki VTM remains a large, government-recognized (Critical Minerals List) strategic resource that could still create option value if a revised consenting pathway or legislative change emerges, at essentially zero cost to current shareholders since it is not in the base valuation
bear_case: Explicit going-concern material uncertainty disclosed in the most recent (H1FY2026) financial statements - net current liabilities of A$21.7m and continued operating cash burn mean execution failure or a metals price pullback could quickly threaten solvency

Taranaki VTM's Fast-track application was effectively refused (draft decline, then withdrawal) - a second failed NZ marine consent attempt for the same project after the 2021 refusal - leaving no clear near-term regulatory path and stranding a large book value of exploration/evaluation assets tied to the project

Heavy and ongoing shareholder dilution (share capital roughly tripled in six months to Dec 2025; ~1.6bn shares outstanding; lender warrants and option exercises add further overhang) erodes per-share value even if the restart succeeds

High-cost, high-leverage capital structure (US$30m Nebari facility plus warrants, substantial finance costs) means a large share of restart cash flow will service debt before benefiting equity holders

Zero analyst/broker coverage, thin trading liquidity, and a two-year track record of no revenue create high execution and valuation uncertainty; restart timelines have already slipped multiple times historically (2022 silver trial ended early, Mt Boppy operations halted Q1 2024) and mine plan capex estimates have already been revised up (A$18.9m to A$26.6m)
